newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey plans to buy 50 airliners for $4 billion.
newsitem.headline: Turkey plans to buy 50 airliners for $4 billion.

text.p: Turkish Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan said on Tuesday Turkey is planning to buy 50 civil aircraft worth a total $4 billion under an offset agreement.
"Turkey needs 100 aircraft. We will buy 50 planes and this costs $4 billion. We will ask for an offset agreement from the supplier," he told his Welfare Party deputies at a meeting.
Erbakan said the government had held talks with senior officials from Airbus last week and would hold talks next week with the chairman of Boeing.
He gave no details on the timing of the agreement or the size of the aircraft that Turkey would buy.
Under the planned offset agreement Turkey would manufacture half of the parts for the civil aircraft, Erbakan said.
A close aide to Erbakan said Turkey would also hold talks with McDonnell Douglas on the plan, which he said would include 50-54 planes.
The aide said Turkish Aerospace Industry, which manufactures military F-16 planes under licence at its plant near Ankara, could produce parts for the civil aircraft.
Turkey's state-owned airline Turkish Airlines (THY) already has 65 aircraft, including three cargo planes. It will lease another Airbus A-340 aircraft this year, THY officials said.
